'''''Blackstonia perfoliata''''' or more commonly known as the '''yellow-wort''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Gentianaceae]] found around the [[Mediterranean Basin]], but extending into northwestern [[Europe]].

==Description==
Yellow-wort grows {{cvt|10-50|cm|in|abbr=on}} tall, with stiff, branching stems. The leaves are [[glaucous]], opposite and entire, the upper ones [[Leaf shape|perfoliate]], being united at the base. It bears terminal [[Cyme (botany)#Determinate|cymes]] of bright yellow, stalked flowers, {{cvt|1-1.5|cm|in|abbr=on}} across. The [[calyx (botany)|calyx]] is deeply divided into 6–10 linear lobes or [[sepal]]s, spirally arranged, free or nearly free from each other at the base and shorter than the [[corolla (botany)|corolla]]. The petals number six to ten and form a short tube. There are six to ten adherent [[stamen]]s and a two-lobed [[Stigma (botany)|stigma]].<ref name=MF>McClintock D. and Fitter, R. ''The Pocket Guide to Wildflowers''. Collins (1956)</ref>

==Ecology==
This species is found in chalk or limestone turf and on dunes. It flowers from June to October in Britain where it is widespread but not common.<ref name=MF/>
Pathogens affecting ''B. perfoliata'' include ''[[Peronospora chlorae]]''.<ref>{{Citation | title = Peronospora chlorae | author = Hall, G. | work = IMI Descriptions of Fungi and Bacteria }}</ref>
